about: Worst-case stack of the Telegram poll task (tg_poll), checked on the built image by check_tg_poll_stack.py. Method and the measured tables: coverage/STACK-2026-11.md. Every row below says why it is true; a row this image does not use is reported as a warning in the report, not a failure (four release images share this config; coverage/STACK-2026-11.md section 2).

fixed_overhead._why: Bytes on the task stack no frame shows. The FreeRTOS Xtensa port (port.c pxPortInitialiseStack) puts the coprocessor save area (XT_CP_SIZE 316 B on the S3, rounded to 16) and the GCC TLS block (9 B of .tdata/.tbss, rounded to 16) at the top of every task stack. An interrupt at the deepest point pushes one exception frame (XT_STK_FRMSZ 192 B) plus the interrupted frame's 16 B base save area before switching to the ISR stack.

recursion.why: a provider response is parsed off the TLS stream with NestingLimit(kResponseNestingLimit = 64) (http.h, transport_tls.cpp execCore, the only device reader given that limit): a reply whose kept part nests 64 deep recurses 64 levels of parseVariant (112 B a level, parseObject and parseArray inlined)

the same limit counts skipped levels too, and a skipped level costs 64 B (skipVariant plus skipObject or skipArray) against a kept level's 112 B: the 64 kept levels above already bound a reply nested 64 deep however much of it the filter drops, so the skip recursion adds no level of its own

ArduinoJson's parse, skip, serialize, copy and clear recurse once per nesting level; the deserializer stops at its nesting limit (ARDUINOJSON_DEFAULT_NESTING_LIMIT 10) and the device builds no deeper document
std::sort: introsort bounds its depth at 2 log2(n); n < 8192 for every list sorted on the device
std::stable_sort: merge recursion depth log2(n), n < 8192

std::stable_partition halves the range per level when its buffer is short: depth <= log2(n)+1. The only caller on tg_poll, router_catalog::protectHeads (router_catalog.h:421), partitions at most kHarvestCollectMax (512) rows: 10 levels
Arduino SD (sd_diskio.cpp:142): an application command first sends APP_CMD (55) through one nested sdCommand call; APP_CMD is not one of the four commands that do, so it nests once
std::map destruction recurses per red-black tree level: height < 2 log2(n+1), maps here hold under 256 entries
strftime recurses once for a composite conversion (%c, %x)
mbedTLS: GCM and CCM run their block cipher through mbedtls_cipher_update on an inner AES-ECB context (one level); the S3 bignum splits an overlong multiply once
lwIP: draining a listening netconn frees its queued connections (one level); lwip_send and lwip_sendto fall back to each other once
libstdc++ error paths: a failure while raising an exception raises once more, then terminates
esp_log's lazy lock creation can log one allocation failure, which takes the lock path once more
a file handle's last reference closes the file, which drops the handle's own shared count once
a cancelled job is metered with one more exchange, which does not cancel again
model-name helpers retry once on a stripped or aliased name
fixOpItem splices an embedded op list only while depth < 2 (orch_turn.cpp fixOpItem, spliceOpList at depth 0): at most three levels
the archive tree is /tgarchive/<chat>/<day>/<item>: four levels
a Telegram file URL is re-resolved once after a 404
openNextFile skips one unreadable entry by calling itself
pinMode detaches the pin's old bus, whose deinit sets the mode once
the subject scan recurses per nesting level of the parsed reply (ArduinoJson limit 10)

allocation and lock re-entry: a failed allocation or a lazily created lock logs, and that log's own allocation or lock can take the same path once more; the second failure is dropped, never logged again

newlib stdio: printing to an unbuffered stream re-enters _vfprintf_r once through __sbprintf on a buffered stand-in (so _vfprintf_r is counted twice, __sbprintf once); closing or flushing a FILE flushes it once; a stream's first write sizes its buffer once (__smakebuf_r, __swhatbuf_r)
IPv6 neighbour discovery: sending a packet to an unresolved neighbour sends one solicitation first
a functor that captures a std::function copies or destroys it through that function's manager; captures nest at most three deep (a tool lambda holding a deps struct holding a hook)
runTurn wraps the head tool dispatch in at most three decorators (the MCP loop tools, pseudo spawns, the claim gate: engine.cpp) over the registry's own dispatch
walks of a provider's JSON tool schema or reply, one level per nesting level (ArduinoJson limit 10)

recursion.function: ^(agent::runsOnText\(|std::function<std::__cxx11::basic_string<char, std::char_traits<char>, std::allocator<char> > \((char const\*|std::__cxx11::basic_string<char, std::char_traits<char>, std::allocator<char> > const&)\)>::operator\(\)|std::_Function_handler<std::__cxx11::basic_string<char, std::char_traits<char>, std::allocator<char> > \((char const\*|std::__cxx11::basic_string<char, std::char_traits<char>, std::allocator<char> > const&)\), (agent::TurnEngine::runTurn|agent::providers::runFabricLoop))
recursion.why: a turn's text hooks (the head host's model text, the fabric's per-host input lead) wrap a hook of the same type once; none calls itself
a round's step is wrapped at most twice over the provider's own step: the same-host resend of an unsent request (resendUnsentOnce) and the fabric's per-host wrap
the turn's speak hook forwards once to the device's speaker hook

impossible_cycles.why: RowTextOverlay wraps the append-log store, never another overlay: its inner_ calls do not reach itself
BlockingClientReader reads the NetworkClient it holds, never itself
RouterTap wraps the TLS transport, never another tap
a void() std::function that reaches its own caller again: the deferred-work and middleware lambdas behind this signature do not call back into the code that runs them
the console VFS forwards to the UART or USB-serial device it wraps, never back to the console
a device's select hook signals the waiting select; it does not run another select
the fabric loop's steps are single-host loop steps (misLoopStep, antLoopStep, ...); none starts another fabric loop

memory::lock logs a slow lock through alogf; alogf reaches memory::lock only through the shared_ptr release the analysis cannot type (every _Sp_counted control block), and alogf's durable write releases only its own file handle (a VFSFileImpl), never the archive's day-zip reader whose destructor takes the loop lock

dynamic_frames.why: char buf[len] for the stored value, up to NVS's 4000 B string limit (Preferences.cpp); settings reads now go through nvsReadStr, which copies into PSRAM

paths.name: turn start (inbound message to the head)
head round, its cut retry included
paths._why: a cut (length) retry runs the same request again inside the same loop step, so it is no deeper than the round

paths.name: provider reply parsed off the TLS stream (64 levels)
claim check correction round
paths._why: the correction is sent as one more head round from runTurn; the check itself is what runs past it

paths.name: OTA check or install, staged on the poll task
paths._why: runOnPoll runs the staged check (checkRun, inlined into it) or install

_unresolved_why: An indirect call no rule, signature or vtable resolves is charged 512 B below it: what is left after the rows below are shallow hooks (UART putc, ring-buffer copies, pin detach callbacks, std::function holding a plain pointer). The report counts them; a deep one must get a row.

terminal.why: never returns: the device restarts. The bytes it takes decide only how the panic reads, so the gate counts its own frame and stops there

impossible_calls.why: its only log is ESP_RETURN_ON_FALSE(out_alignment, ..., "null pointer") (esp_mm/esp_cache_msync.c), and its only caller here, esp_heap_adjust_alignment_to_hw, passes the address of a local
every TLS context on the device is a client: ssl_client.cpp's mbedtls_ssl_config_defaults(..., MBEDTLS_SSL_IS_CLIENT, ...); the server step runs only for MBEDTLS_SSL_IS_SERVER

renegotiation stays at mbedTLS's default MBEDTLS_SSL_RENEGOTIATION_DISABLED: nothing in the firmware or its libraries calls mbedtls_ssl_conf_renegotiation, and both callers return before renegotiating when it is disabled

read and write run the handshake only on a context whose handshake is not over; ssl_client.cpp start_ssl_client finishes the handshake (or fails the connect) before any read or write, and renegotiation is off

_aliases_why: Typedefs and macros the source uses for a class: FileImplPtr and FSImplPtr are shared_ptrs of fs::FileImpl and fs::FSImpl (FS.h); WiFiClient(Secure) are the Arduino 3 names of NetworkClient(Secure); Serial is HWCDCSerial on these boards (ARDUINO_USB_CDC_ON_BOOT=1, ARDUINO_USB_MODE=1 in platformio.ini)

stdout_context.why: printf, puts and esp_log write the console stream (stdout, fd 1, the console VFS over USB serial or UART); a file write never runs below them, so inside that stream's stdio calls the VFS reaches the console devices only
